pr_title: Apply hosting environment via command line args
pr_body:
- This makes sure that the entire application can see changes to host configuration (env, content root etc).
- Added tests to verify those scenarios
- One caveat is that the application can still override the test values manually (fore.g not passing the args)

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/33889

issue_context.title: WebApplicationFactory<T> does not default to Development environment with minimal hosting
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Compared to the use cases for `IHostBuilder` and `IWebHostBuilder`, `WebApplicationFactory<T>` does not set the default environment for the application under test to `Development` when the code path for minimal hosting is used.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9a451a36297f5e24f40b08ce59bfdb1f8f287ea0/src/Mvc/Mvc.Testing/src/WebApplicationFactory.cs#L383

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/dbf84eaa5a8f79947647ad64a785d39e7cd23afe/src/Mvc/Mvc.Testing/src/WebApplicationFactory.cs#L402

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/dbf84eaa5a8f79947647ad64a785d39e7cd23afe/src/Mvc/Mvc.Testing/src/WebApplicationFactory.cs#L152-L178

Adding the missing line itself does not seem to work though, possibly related to #33876 - ~I've got some tests from debugging this locally I'll push up into a PR shortly~ see #33890.

### To Reproduce

Inspect the `IHostEnvironment.EnvironmentName` property in, for example, the [`HelloWorld`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9a451a36297f5e24f40b08ce59bfdb1f8f287ea0/src/Mvc/test/Mvc.FunctionalTests/SimpleWithWebApplicationBuilderTests.cs#L21-L32) test.

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/9a451a36297f5e24f40b08ce59bfdb1f8f287ea0/src/Mvc/test/Mvc.FunctionalTests/SimpleWithWebApplicationBuilderTests.cs#L21-L32

### Further technical details

* ASP.NET Core `6.0.0-preview.6.21323.4`
* .NET SDK `6.0.100-preview.6.21324.1`
* Visual Studio 2022 17.0.0 Preview 1.1

review_comments: Do we need to do any fancy escaping for `value`? Like can values have spaces which would break config parsing? I'm not super familiar with this area

I don't see how it breaks given how the [parsing works](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/cf52b7e38d28b7e28358cee052effe0ed47efb2e/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.CommandLine/src/CommandLineConfigurationProvider.cs#L44). We're not parsing the command line string, we're parsing each arg. 

I also don't see a way to escape `-` or `/` so that might be the only problem.
An `=` in the key would also mess this up, right? I'm not sure how realistic that is.

> I also don't see a way to escape - or / so that might be the only problem.

You could always base64 encode/decode. Stripping and adding back the `=` padding characters might be a pain though.
I think we wait until somebody hits this then we fix it by supporting escape sequences in the command line configuration provider, the problem is general.

This is the bug being fixed. We do it in the other 2 cases but not in this one 
1. https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/18a926850f7374248e687ee64390e7f10514403f/src/Mvc/Mvc.Testing/src/WebApplicationFactory.cs#L384
2. https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/18a926850f7374248e687ee64390e7f10514403f/src/Mvc/Mvc.Testing/src/WebApplicationFactory.cs#L403
